competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every sample directly exercises the core requirement of estimating products using multiples of 10. For instance, in "Estimate the product: 120 × 14", the student rounds 14 to 10 to obtain 120 × 10 = 1200. In "Estimate the product: 32 × 15", factors round to 30 × 20 = 600. Cloze formats like "Estimate: 20 × 14 ≈ ___" and error verification items like "Grace solved: "150 × 13 ≈ ___". Grace says the missing number is 1500. Is Grace correct?" directly target the required skill.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample packet thoroughly covers the range of factor combinations specified in the competency. It includes 2-digit by 2-digit multiplication cases such as "Estimate the product: 10 × 32", "Estimate the product: 48 × 30", and "Rico solved: "67 × 76 ≈ ___". Rico says the missing number is 5600. Is Rico correct?", as well as 3-digit by 2-digit scenarios such as "Estimate the product: 120 × 14", "Estimate: 930 × 13 ≈ ___", "Estimate the product: 853 × 12", and "Estimate the product: 100 × 14".

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The difficulty and structural complexity are well-calibrated for Grade 3 Quarter 3 learners. Items like "Estimate: 20 × 14 ≈ ___" and "Estimate the product: 11 × 45" require straightforward rounding to the nearest ten and multiplying by tens, which is fully aligned with Grade 3 cognitive development and avoids unneeded procedural or reading overload.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The items utilize a diverse array of assessment formatters, including standard multiple choice ("Estimate the product: 120 × 14"), cloze fill-ins ("Estimate: 20 × 14 ≈ ___"), truth-value verification ("19 × 30 ≈ 592. True or False?"), and error detection/critique (Liza solved: "21 × 30 ≈ ___". Liza says the missing number is 600. Is Liza correct?).

competency_alignment.rationale: The problems strictly align with the MATATAG learning competency without introducing any out-of-scope operations or higher-grade concepts. Every item, such as "Estimate the product: 853 × 12" and "Estimate: 10 × 45 ≈ ___", centers on estimating factor products using multiples of 10 without exceeding the specified digit limits.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical magnitudes across all samples strictly obey the bounds of 2- to 3-digit numbers multiplied by 1- to 2-digit numbers. Examples range from 2-digit combinations in "Estimate the product: 40 × 30" and "Estimate: 20 × 35 ≈ ___" to 3-digit by 2-digit combinations in "Estimate the product: 853 × 12" and "Estimate: 930 × 13 ≈ ___".
